J U D G M E N T

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of .5,00,000/- along with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., he was going along with his father, mother and brother on Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-08-Q-4133 while travelling from Mudaram Doddi to their village, a Hyundai Eon Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motor cycle.

Due to the accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, he was shifted to Government Hospital, V.Kota and later shifted to PES Hospital, Kuppam, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was 04 years old.
Due to the accidental injuries, petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver.
The respondent, being the owner of the offending vehicle, is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. The respondent not engaged the services of counsel in spite of granting sufficient opportunities and hence, respondent is considered to be contesting the petitioner in her individual capacity.
Respondent not filed the written statement in spite of according opportunities and as such, written statement of respondent is treated nil.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:
POINTS 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., near at Bangla vuru village, V.Kota Mandalam, on V.Kota- Pernumbat Road, Chittor District, AP, when petitioner was traveling on a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.NO.KA-08-Q-4133, as a pillion rider, due to the rash and negligent driving of Hyundai Eon Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver?

2 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3
. What order or award?

5. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the natural guardian/father of petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got examined Medical Record Officer at PES Hospital, Kuppam,
Chittoor District as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his side evidence.
The respondent not adduced evidence on her behalf.
6. Heard the argument of counsel for petitioner.
Argument of respondent is treated nil.
Perused the materials available on record.

The petitioner contended that on 19.05.2024 at about 03.45 p.m., accident occurred near Bangla vuru village, V.Kota-Pernumbat Road, Chittor District, AP, when petitioner was riding his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-08-Q-4133, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
9. Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.2, first information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, one of relatives of petitioner by name Sri.D.M.Venkataramana S/o Late Muneppa has lodged complaint with police on 20.05.2024 pertaining to the accident occurred on 19.05.2024.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P1 discloses the aspect of registration of FIR against the driver of offending car.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex . P1
discloses the aspect of registration of FIR against the driver of offending car.

The petitioner also furnished copy of spot sketch and its translated version,
which is marked as Ex.P.3 and P.3(a).
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.

The respondent not placed any satisfactory materials in order to show that the facts at the place of Nehanth vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97280757/
3 accident, as described in the sketch, are contrary to the actual facts.
The sketch discloses the aspect of occurrence of accident in the route in which the petitioner has been travelling.
The sketch furnished by petitioner discloses that the offending vehicle came to right side in which the petitioner is going.
The sketch furnished by petitioner also discloses the aspect of negligence on the part of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.337 & 338 and Sec.146 R/w.196 of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.6.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondent to show that the investigation is not conducted in proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.

10. The natural guardian and father of petitioner got examined as PW.1 and filed the affidavit in lieu of chief examination wherein he stated the aspect of occurrence of accident due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondent, though appeared before the Tribunal, not cross examined PW.1 in order to rebut or controvert the contention of petitioner.
The evidence of PW.1 remains unrebutted and unchallenged.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
11. The respondent not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondent not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.6, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
12. Point No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during the treatment, disability, loss of amenities.

4 13.

The Natural Guardian of minor petitioner contended that due to accident his son sustained injuries like degloving laceration measuring 5x3x3 cm noted in left side of face below the orbit extending upto tempee and all over the body.

In order to prove the injuries sustained by the petitioner, he has produced wound certificate issued by PES Institute of Medical Sciences &
Research Hospital, Bengaluru marked at Ex.P.4.

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P.4 it reveals that, the petitioner sustained degloving laceration measuring 5x3x3 cm noted in left side of face below the orbit extending upto tempee and all over the body and doctor opined that injury is simple in nature.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.5 - discharge summary issued by PES University Hospital to show that he has taken treatment as an inpatient on 27.05.2024 & 28.05.2024 i.e., for a period of 02 days.

The doctor diagnosed that petitioner has sustained sutured laceration of size 10x4x3 cms noted over left side of the cheek and eyelid and underwent procedure for removal of under IV Sedation and later discharge.
The petitioner has also produced medical bills amounting to .54,277/- marked at Ex.P.7.
The amount mentioned in the advance receipts is included in the discharge bills furnished by petitioner.

The two discharge bills furnished by petitioner disclose that the amount mentioned in advance receipts have been deducted in the discharge bill and balance amount has been received from the petitioner.
The discharge bill discloses that the expenses incurred by petitioner for treatment is .54,277/-.
The amount mentioned in the advance receipts has been deducted from the total bill amount.
As such, the medical expenses is considered to be .54,277/-.
The respondent not furnished satisfactory materials to rebut or disbelieve the medical bills furnished by petitioner.
In order to prove disability, the petitioner neither produced disability certificate nor examined the doctor.

Further the petitioner examined the Medical Record Officer at PES Hospital, Kuppam,
Chittoor District, A.P. as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.9 to 13 i.e., authorization letter,
MLC Register Extract, Police Intimation, case sheet and X-ray films.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the aspect of disability.
The evidence of PW.2 does not disclose the aspect of disability sustained by petitioner.
Evidence of PW.2 is not sufficient and satisfactory in order to assess and ascertain the aspect of disability sustained by petitioner.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the disability sustained by him.
The petitioner neither examined any witness nor furnished any materials in order to ascertain the disability stated to have been sustained by him.
The petitioner also not furnished any materials in order to show loss of education due to the accidental injuries.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to consider the impact and effect of accidental injuries to his future.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that the accidental injuries affected the petitioner in carrying out normal activities and caused disability to him.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .1,50,000/- (including medical bills).
14.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 15. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.TN-18-AH-5595 by its driver.

Nehanth vs Suriyaprabha K on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97280757/
5
The materials on record disclose that the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective policy of insurance at the time of accident.
In the absence of valid insurance policy, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
So, the respondent, being the owner of the offending vehicle, is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Point No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Point No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said points, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of MV Act is allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of .1,50,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

Entire compensation amount shall be kept in FD in the name of minor petitioner in any of the Nationalized Bank or Scheduled Bank of the choice of minor guardian for a period of 3 years or till he attain the age of majority whichever is later.
The guardian of petitioner is entitled to receive interest that accrues on FD periodically.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to his account after expiry of three years period of deposit, without waiting for further order of court.
Advocates' fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
